corpus_counts.note: candidate counts are phase-1 only; the ubi9 figure is inflated by Red Hat cross-stream matches — see decisions.redhat_two_phase. empty entries are SBOM components without a purl (files, relationships, document nodes); they are never submitted anywhere.

decisions.request_shape: Always query OSV in ecosystem form ({package:{name,ecosystem},version}), never purl form. Three live findings force this: (1) Alpine purl queries return {} even for known-vulnerable versions (pkg:apk/alpine/busybox@1.36.1-r0 -> {}, ecosystem form -> 7 advisories); (2) purl queries evaluate every distribution stream, producing cross-stream false positives (pkg:deb/debian/glibc@2.36-9+deb12u1 purl-form 39 vs stream-scoped Debian:12 form 35); (3) rpm purls carry epoch as a qualifier Syft emits separately, and ignoring it makes Red Hat matching wildly wrong (openssl 1.1.1k-7.el8 without epoch: 115 advisories including 2014-era; with 1: epoch folded in: 54).
decisions.classification_rule: Deterministic, adapter-side, applied before any query is issued: no purl -> empty; purl fails to parse or percent-decode -> invalid; parsed purl without version -> unversioned; (type,namespace) outside the proven mapping table, or apk/deb purl without the distro qualifier that selects the OSV stream -> unsupported, with reason; otherwise queryable with the translated ecosystem-form query. The mapping table IS the supported-ecosystem list; OSV returns {} for unsupported ecosystems (probed pkg:rpm/amzn openssl: {}), indistinguishable from supported-with-zero-findings, so classification can never be inferred from responses. Unversioned purls must never be submitted: a versionless query returns the package's entire advisory history (pkg:apk/alpine/busybox -> 30 advisories).
decisions.redhat_two_phase: Red Hat OSV records key streams as ecosystem strings with unguessable variants (Red Hat:enterprise_linux:8::baseos, Red Hat:enterprise_linux:10.0, Red Hat:enterprise_linux_eus:10.0, Red Hat:hummingbird:1), so no single ecosystem string can be derived from a Syft purl (distro=rhel-9.8 gives major.minor, never the variant). Rule: phase 1 queries ecosystem 'Red Hat' (name, epoch-folded version) for candidates; phase 2 fetches each candidate record (needed anyway for severity and ranges), keeps affected entries whose package.name matches and whose ecosystem parses to the same enterprise_linux major as the distro qualifier, and re-queries with that entry's exact ecosystem string; the finding is confirmed only when the advisory id comes back from the stream-scoped query. Version semantics stay server-side; the adapter owns no rpm version comparator. Live proof: fully patched ubi9 glibc 2.34-275.el9_8 had 11 phase-1 candidates, all el10/hummingbird streams, and 0 survived phase 2.
decisions.fixed_version_projection: From the confirmed record, take affected entries matching the queried (ecosystem string, name); collect the 'fixed' events of their ranges. Exactly one distinct fixed value (the overwhelmingly common case, e.g. RHSA-2023:7877 el8 baseos: [introduced 0, fixed 1:1.1.1k-12.el8_9]) projects as-is. Multiple distinct values are all stored verbatim and displayed as the full set sorted lexicographically for stability — the adapter never invents a semantic 'minimum' across ranges because that would require a per-ecosystem version comparator it deliberately does not own. Ranges with only last_affected events (e.g. GHSA-78h2-9frx-2jm8's go-jose v2 entry) project as no-fix-available.
decisions.severity: OSV severity arrives as severity[] CVSS vectors (CVSS_V3/CVSS_V4 type + vector string, no numeric score), sometimes plus database_specific.severity qualitative labels (GHSA: 'HIGH') and ecosystem_specific.urgency (Debian). All are stored verbatim with the record; the fixed display scale is derived (qualitative label preferred, else CVSS base score banded, else unknown). Some records carry no severity at all (GO-2026-4945: severity null) — unknown is a first-class display state.
decisions.batch_behavior: POST /v1/querybatch accepts up to 1000 queries; 593 real-corpus queries completed in two chunks of <=500 in ~1.4s total with zero next_page_token. One malformed query fails the ENTIRE batch with a single code-3 error naming the query index. Because classification runs before batching, a batch error can only mean an adapter bug: the run fails closed rather than papering over it.
decisions.go_version_prefix: Immaterial: golang.org/x/crypto queried as v0.16.0 and 0.16.0 return identical 38 advisories. Versions pass through as Syft emits them.
decisions.osv_first: OSV.dev is the MVP provider. api.osv.dev serves Red Hat data (stale docs omit it; the API is ground truth) sourced from Red Hat's own CSAF/VEX-derived OSV feed (every RHSA record's database_specific.source points at https://security.access.redhat.com/data/osv/...), so backport-awareness is inherited by construction. Red Hat's direct feed (https://security.access.redhat.com/data/osv/all.json) is recorded as fallback evidence only — not an MVP adapter, not a config surface.
decisions.database_revision: No query, querybatch, or vulns response carries a database snapshot identifier; per-record 'modified' timestamps are the only versioning. Recorded as the accepted 'database_revision unreported' rider.
